# Overview {#sec-overview}

## What Excel-AI is

Excel-AI is the Excel side of the CPAT-AI project: Excel prototypes of legacy CPAT, written by Python builders (openpyxl) and checked by LibreOffice recalculation and independent Python recomputation, for modellers and reviewers who work in Excel and for the CPAT team. Its files are in `excel_ai/`.

- **Modules.** One workbook per module, without macros (since 1.2.0): mitigation (the integrated model), distribution and air pollution.
- **The Master workbook.** `excel_ai/master/CPAT-AI-MT_latest.xlsm (the MT, Multiscenario Tool; activated as `excel_ai/active_workbooks/CPAT-AI-MT.xlsb`)` holds every macro: it activates the modules (formulas to 2041, saved as `.xlsb`), updates their data tables (Power Query, the country or all countries) and the distribution inputs, runs every country with every scenario, keeps the results as values and compares them in tables and charts (@sec-workbooks).
- **Releases.** Mitigation and the Master 1.5.1; Distribution 0.5.1, on its own 0.x line (0.1.0-0.1.4, then 0.2.0-0.2.3, 0.3.0, 0.4.0-0.4.2, 0.5.0-0.5.1, following the Mitigation releases 1.0.0 to 1.3.1). One line per release: `excel_ai/core/CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Inputs.** The policy and parameter inputs are the rows and names of the legacy `MTInputs` sheet (`NameOfParameter`), in legacy units. The codes map ([`excel_ai/core/CPAT-AI_CodesMap_latest.xlsx`](https://github.com/cpmodelai/cpat_ai/raw/main/excel_ai/core/CPAT-AI_CodesMap_latest.xlsx), tab Inputs) lists every input with its row, its name, its legacy name and its Python key.
- **Codes and data.** Input codes, output codes and the sector and fuel vocabularies are shared with the Python model (the *CPAT Python* tab), which replicates Excel-AI number for number. Both read the root folder `data/` (@sec-data).
- **The rule** on bugs and issues (@sec-bugs).

## Legacy CPAT: the reference

The legacy workbook is the ground truth for both models. The latest version, 1.0pre_465, is kept read-only in `data/` (the earlier NoPropData copies of 456, 459 and 465 are no longer in the repository):

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `data/legacy/CPAT 1.0pre_465_Shell.xlsb` | The legacy CPAT workbook with its six proprietary tabs empty (every other tab filled); the reference for input rows and names, and for the register's cell references |
| `data/Public01/legacy/CPAT 1.0pre_465_Public01.xlsb` | The shell filled with data edition Public01's tables (the proprietary ones perturbed) |

The legacy workbook is never edited or re-saved; work is done on copies in scratch folders.

## How the work proceeds

1. **Replicate.** A block of legacy CPAT is rebuilt in the prototype, formula by formula, with the same sections and the same codes.
2. **Check.** An independent Python recomputation of the block reproduces every number; the prototype's result is compared with legacy's stored results.
3. **Classify every difference.** A difference is either a legacy bug (fixed in the prototype, with a cell-level fix plan for legacy), a legacy issue (replicated and tracked), or a departure decided by the team (tracked).
4. **Release.** The builder writes a new version; the quick check, the paste test and the regression against the previous release must pass; the register documents, the tracker, the codes map and the decks are regenerated.
5. **Port.** Validated blocks are ported to the Python model (the *CPAT Python* tab).

## Status of the modules

| Module | Status |
|---|---|
| Mitigation: prices, power, transport, buildings, industry, emissions, ETS, revenues, GDP, welfare | Integrated prototype, released |
| Distribution: household effects by decile | Standalone module, released on its own version line (0.5.1; its formulas cut from the mitigation builder) |
| Air pollution | Standalone workbook: data scaffold built, calculations open |
| Road transport co-benefits | Values typed into the prototype from the module (tab `FromTrans`) |

## How the workbooks work {#sec-workbooks}

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `excel_ai/master/CPAT-AI-MT_latest.xlsm (the MT, Multiscenario Tool; activated as `excel_ai/active_workbooks/CPAT-AI-MT.xlsb`)` | **The Master**: open it first (Excel 365, macros on). Tab `Dashboard`: the core macros, the countries and scenarios to run, the data choices; tab `Activation and Macros`: every other macro, explained, the module table and the data sources; the master scenario table and the stored results |
| `excel_ai/<module>/<Name>_latest.xlsx` | The latest **unactivated** module: no macros, formulas to 2035 (small, quick to open), with the values of the full model |
| `excel_ai/active_workbooks/<Name>_latest.xlsb` | The **activated** module, written by the Master: formulas to 2041, recalculated. Work here |
| `excel_ai/<module>/releases/<Name>_v<version>.xlsx` | Every version (to 1.1.0: `<Name>-Prototype_v<version>.xlsm`, with macros) |
| `excel_ai/master/` | The Master's builder and its VBA (`CPATMaster.bas`) |

1. **Activate all.** On the Master's `Dashboard`, *Activate all* opens each module's `.xlsx` (from the clone, else GitHub), copies the 2035 column across to 2041 in every scenario group of `Mitigation` and `Outputs`, adds the live scenario groups (four by default), writes the Master's scenario table into the module, recalculates and saves `<Name>_latest.xlsb` next to the Master. Calculation is automatic.
2. **Choose the countries and the scenarios** on the Master's `Dashboard`: one country per row and one scenario ID per row (`BASE` the baseline, `P1`-`P5` the presets, `U1`, `U2`, ... user scenarios; the IDs of the Master's tab `Scenarios`, the rows of legacy MTInputs), and the data source and rows. Every country listed runs every scenario listed. *Update data* loads the linked data tabs by Power Query (all countries, for a run of many).
3. **Run scenarios.** The Master runs the list in batches over the live scenario groups 2-4 of the mitigation workbook (the baseline once per country; ETS scenarios with their goal seek, one per group) and stores every run as values in `StoredResults`.
4. **Read the results.** Live, in the mitigation workbook: tab `Dashboard` (the country and the policy scenario chosen by name, key numbers and charts), `Outputs` (the live scenario groups side by side, one output code per row, in Mitigation's row order within each topic; code `variable.sector.fuel.suffix`, with the country in front and the scenario number at the end; cost components `cost.<sector>.<fuel>.<component>`) and `Diagnostic` (the country's baseline). Stored, in the Master: `StoredResults`, `Scenario comparison`, `OneCountry` and `ManyCountries`. Tab `Docs & Versions` of the module holds the version log, the differences with legacy, the variable dictionary and the LAMBDAs.
5. **Other macros** (tab `Activation and Macros`): *Send scenario to Mitigation*, *Get live scenario*, *Sync scenarios to Mitigation*, *Store live scenarios*, *Estimate run time*, *Goal-seek ETS price*, *Achieve NDCs*, *Distribution from Mitigation* (the export block, section 11a, into the distribution workbook), *Save results to .csv* and others, each with what it does.

**Speed.** The modules ship with their calculated values and formulas to 2035, so they open quickly; repeated formulas are stored once as shared formulas; the activated workbook is a binary `.xlsb`; calculation is automatic.

**Next steps.** A user interface (its specification, a mock-up and the core graphs of country reports, is in `excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/ui_spec/`); model settings split from policy inputs; the other modules (distribution started; air pollution; transport co-benefits); the full set of core graphs in the Master (which replaces the legacy Multiscenario Tool, kept in `excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/legacy_multiscenario_tool/`); the real data behind the dummy panels of the Dashboard and the Diagnostic.

The `.xlsb` are generated files: on a git conflict take either side and activate again; never merge them, and never commit Excel's `~$` lock files. A workbook run with real data stays on your local drive. The release notes are in the task log (`excel_ai/core/CAVEATS.md`). Details: @sec-mitigation and @sec-many-scenarios.

## Bugs and issues {#sec-bugs}

::: {.callout-important}
#### The rule

**Never replicate a legacy bug; always replicate a legacy issue, and track it.**
:::

The rule applies to every model of the project, in Excel and in Python. It keeps the prototypes faithful to legacy CPAT where legacy does what it means to, and correct where it does not, and it makes every difference from legacy visible.

### Definitions

| Kind | Code | Meaning | What the prototype does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Legacy bug | L | Legacy does not compute what it means to: a wrong row, a double application, a dead reference | Fixes it, never replicates it; the fix is written up as a cell-level plan for legacy |
| Prototype bug | M | A bug found in the prototype itself | Fixes it and records it |
| Documentation bug | DOC | An error in the CPAT methodology documentation | Corrects it in the methodology's chapter *Corrections* |
| Major issue, data | MId | One of the five most important data issues (MId1-MId5) | As an issue: replicates it and tracks it |
| Major issue, methodology | MIm | One of the five most important open questions of method (MIm1-MIm5) | As an issue: replicates it and tracks it |
| Issue | I | Legacy does what it means to, but the choice is open to question | Does the same as legacy and tracks it |
| Departure | LD | A deliberate difference from legacy that is not a bug fix | Kept only by decision of the team; tracked in the prototype's `LegacyDiff` sheet |
| Upgrade | U | A feature beyond legacy | Tracked |

The ten major issues were issues (I) first; the register keeps their former codes (MId1-MId5: I90, I97, I98, I91, I92; MIm1-MIm5: I71, I62, I31, I41, I113).

**Data problems are issues.** They are replicated. Where legacy needs a formula fix to handle the data correctly, that fix is a legacy bug (L) with a cell plan and the issue is ranked *Very high*; where no cell plan is possible, the prototype aligns with legacy exactly and the issue is ranked *Extremely high*.

### The register

Every bug and issue lives in one register, the single source from which the documents are generated:

| Document | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/Legacy_CPAT_Bugs_v<version>.docx` | The legacy bugs, each with its cell-level fix plan, and the data problems by priority |
| `excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/Tracking_Legacy_Bugs_v<version>.xlsx` | The master list of bugs and issues, every module, in the same columns; shared with the CPAT team |
| `excel_ai/core/BUGS.md`, `excel_ai/core/ISSUES.md` | The two short lists |
| `excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/register/Legacy_CPAT_Register.json` | The register as data |

The register is written in `excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/register/issues_register.py` and `register.py`; `make_documentation.py` regenerates every document from it at each release.

### Current counts

{{< include _counts.md >}}

The status *Legacy 465* records whether the CPAT team has fixed each bug in the latest legacy workbook; each claimed fix is checked against the workbook (`excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/fixes/check465/`).

### Priorities

Issues and data problems are ranked so the most urgent are seen first: *Extremely high* and *Very high* for data problems (as defined above), then *Major* and *Minor*. Bugs carry *High*, *Medium* or *Low* by their effect on results.
